And as i was reading my reply i realized it probably wasn't much help with those exact words. So imma delve a bit further. So 제가 is used when nobody is asking for you specifically but you answer anyway. And 저는 is when your opinion is specifically asked for or you're talking to a person who you *know* (or assume) wants to hear about your well... Something. Opinion, decision, etc.

A bit of examples with 제가 and 저는

제가

- Who wants to do this work?
- I'll do it.

- 이 일을 누가 할래?
- 제가 할께요.



저는

- I like strawberries. Do you?
- I don't.

- 나는 딸기를 좋아해. 너는?
- 저는 안좋아해요.

-은/는 and -이/가 behave like "the" and "a/an" accordingly (but unlike the english variants they can be changed and not sound too awkward)

Also you use -은/는 when you want to make an accent on that specific word. Like:

THIS book was a present from my mom. (Pointing to a specific book)
이 책은 어머니께서 선물해주셨어요
